question:
Select the option that is related to the sixth letter cluster in the same way as the first letter cluster is related to the second letter cluster and third letter cluster is related to fourth letter cluster.

QH : TL :: BI : EM :: ? : UD
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. RZ.

GIVEN

• QH : TL :: BI : EM :: ? : UD

SOLUTION

• Rule (1st→2nd cluster): 1st letter +3, 2nd letter +4 (cyclic).

• Check QH→TL: Q(17)+3=T(20), H(8)+4=L(12). ✓

• Check BI→EM: B(2)+3=E(5), I(9)+4=M(13). ✓

• Apply to ?→UD: ?+3=U(21) → 1st = 21−3 = 18 = R; ?+4=D(4) → 2nd = 26 (since Z+4 = 26+4 = 30 = 4 = D) = Z.

• So ? = RZ.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Add +3 to the first letter and +4 to the second letter of the answer to reach UD: R+3=U, Z+4=D (wrap-around).

NOTE

• Use position numbers A=1…Z=26 and wrap past 26 back to 1 (cyclic) for such coding-analogy clusters.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

HI, ?, ZW, VQ, RK, NE, JY, FS
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. DC.

GIVEN

• HI, ?, ZW, VQ, RK, NE, JY, FS

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: H, ?, Z, V, R, N, J, F → each −4 (cyclic): H(8), then 8−4=4=D, then D→Z (4−4=0→26), Z(26),V(22),R(18),N(14),J(10),F(6). ✓

• 2nd letters: I, ?, W, Q, K, E, Y, S → each −6 (cyclic): I(9), then 9−6=3=C, then C→W (3−6=−3→23), W(23),Q(17),K(11),E(5),Y(25),S(19). ✓

• Missing term = DC.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• First column drops by 4, second column drops by 6 each step; step back one from HI: H−4=D, I−6=C → DC.

NOTE

• In two-letter series, treat each column separately with position numbers and wrap below 1 by adding 26.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

PV, KP, FJ, ?, VX, QR, LL, GF
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. AD.

GIVEN

• PV, KP, FJ, ?, VX, QR, LL, GF

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: P, K, F, ?, V, Q, L, G → each −5 (cyclic): P(16),K(11),F(6), then 6−5=1=A, then A→V (1−5=−4→22), V(22),Q(17),L(12),G(7). ✓

• 2nd letters: V, P, J, ?, X, R, L, F → each −6 (cyclic): V(22),P(16),J(10), then 10−6=4=D, then D→X (4−6=−2→24), X(24),R(18),L(12),F(6). ✓

• Missing term = AD.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Column 1 falls by 5, column 2 falls by 6: from FJ → F−5=A, J−6=D → AD.

NOTE

• Constant differences per column; keep wrapping cyclically (add 26 when you go below A).

question:
In the following question, set of letter clusters are given. The letter clusters of each set are related to the letter clusters of the same set by some Logic/Rule/Relation. From the given alternatives, select a group of letter clusters which follows the same Logic/Rule/Relation.

(HR, AK, ZP)

(LO, EH, VS)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. (EV, XO, CL).

GIVEN

• (HR, AK, ZP) and (LO, EH, VS)

SOLUTION

• Rule: within a set, the two letters of every cluster have the same gap.

• (HR,AK,ZP): H→R = 10, A→K = 10, Z→P = 10. All gap 10. ✓

• (LO,EH,VS): L→O = 3, E→H = 3, V→S = 3. All gap 3. ✓

• Check option (EV,XO,CL): E→V = 9 (cyclic, 5+9=14... actually V(22)→E via +9), X→O = 9, C→L = 9. All gap 9. ✓

• Options 1,3,4 have unequal internal gaps.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Just check if all three clusters in an option keep the SAME letter-gap; only (EV, XO, CL) does (gap 9 each).

NOTE

• Measure gaps cyclically (mod 26) — the smaller circular distance between the two letters.

question: If the month of May 2016 ended on Sunday, then which date was the first Monday of October 2016?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 5.

GIVEN

• May 2016 ended (31 May) on Sunday.

SOLUTION

• 31 May = Sun. Odd days: June(30)=+2 → 30 Jun = Tue; July(31)=+3 → 31 Jul = Fri; Aug(31)=+3 → 31 Aug = Mon; Sep(30)=+2 → 30 Sep = Wed.

• So 1 Oct = Thu. Then 2=Fri, 3=Sat, 4=Sun, 5 = Mon.

• First Monday of October 2016 = 5th.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Carry only odd days (days mod 7) month-to-month: +2,+3,+3,+2 lands 30 Sep on Wed, so 1 Oct = Thu → first Monday = 5.

NOTE

• Odd days: 30-day month = 2, 31-day month = 3; add them to the known weekday.

question: If the month of July 2018 ended on Tuesday, then which date was the first Wednesday of December 2018?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 5.

GIVEN

• July 2018 ended (31 July) on Tuesday.

SOLUTION

• 31 Jul = Tue. Aug(31)=+3 → 31 Aug = Fri; Sep(30)=+2 → 30 Sep = Sun; Oct(31)=+3 → 31 Oct = Wed; Nov(30)=+2 → 30 Nov = Fri.

• So 1 Dec = Sat. Then 2=Sun, 3=Mon, 4=Tue, 5 = Wed.

• First Wednesday of December 2018 = 5th.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Add odd days +3,+2,+3,+2 from 31 Jul (Tue) → 30 Nov = Fri, so 1 Dec = Sat → first Wednesday = 5.

NOTE

• Track weekday of each month-end using odd days (31→3, 30→2) instead of counting all dates.

question: Which of the following pairs of years have identical calendars?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 1981 and 1987.

GIVEN

• Find the pair of years with identical calendars.

SOLUTION

• Two years share a calendar when total odd days between them = 0 (mod 7) and both are of the same leap/non-leap type.

• From 1981 to 1987, count odd days of 1981–1986: 1(1981)+1(1982)+1(1983)+2(1984 leap)+1(1985)+1(1986) = 7 ≡ 0.

• 1981 and 1987 are both non-leap years, so their calendars are identical.

• Other pairs give a non-zero remainder or mismatch in leap status.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• A non-leap year repeats its calendar after +6 or +11 years; 1981+6 = 1987 (one leap year, 1984, falls in between making 7 odd days).

NOTE

• Sum odd days (normal = 1, leap = 2) between the years; a multiple of 7 with same leap-type means identical calendars.

question: 5 boys R, S, M, N and P are sitting in a row facing north (not necessarily in the same order). Only N is sitting between S and P. R is to the immediate left of S. R is at one of the end of the row. Who is sitting to the right of P?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. M.

GIVEN

• 5 boys R, S, M, N, P face north. Only N is between S and P. R is immediately left of S. R is at an end.

SOLUTION

• Facing north: left = west, right = east. R is at an end AND immediately left of S → R is the leftmost. So position1 = R, position2 = S.

• Only N between S and P → S, N, P consecutive: position2=S, position3=N, position4=P.

• Remaining M takes position5.

• Order (left→right): R, S, N, P, M.

• Right of P (position4) = position5 = M.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Anchor R at the left end; R–S fixed, then S–N–P block gives R S N P M, so P's right neighbour is M.

NOTE

• For a row facing north, the person's right is towards the east (right side of the drawn row).

question: 7 women A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing towards the centre (not necessarily in the same order). F is second to the right of C. A is third to the left of C. G is third to the left of F. D is not next to F. B is not next to A. Who are the immediate neighbours of C?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. B and G.

GIVEN

• 7 women A–G around a circle facing centre. F = 2nd right of C; A = 3rd left of C; G = 3rd left of F; D not next to F; B not next to A.

SOLUTION

• Facing centre: right = anticlockwise, left = clockwise. Fix C. F = 2 seats anticlockwise of C; A = 3 seats clockwise of C; G = 3 seats clockwise of F.

• This gives the order (clockwise): C, G, D, A, E, F, B and back to C.

• Remaining seats: D not beside F and B not beside A force D and B into their spots, E fills the last.

• Immediate neighbours of C = G and B.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Place C, then F (2 right) and A (3 left), then G (3 left of F) lands right next to C; the 'not-next-to' clues seat B on C's other side.

NOTE

• When people face the centre, 'to the right' means anticlockwise and 'to the left' means clockwise.

question: Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. the square with a diamond (square rotated 45°) inside it.

GIVEN

• A figure analogy: 1st figure : 2nd figure :: 3rd figure : ?

SOLUTION

• Across the analogy each box carries the same outer square; the inner content changes but the outer boundary stays a plain square.

• The answer must be a plain square containing exactly one clean inner shape (matching the style of the given figures).

• Among the options only Option shows a square with a single inscribed diamond, following the same square-with-inner-shape pattern; options 1, 2, 3 (circle, triangle, pentagon) break the required inner-shape relation.

• Hence the missing figure = Option.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Fix the outer boundary first, then match the inner element's symmetry — the diamond-in-square keeps the four-fold symmetry demanded by the series.

NOTE

• In figure analogies, separate the outer frame from the inner element and track each independently.

question: Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. the square with a downward (\) diagonal line carrying three equally-spaced circles.

GIVEN

• Figure analogy: 1st figure : 2nd figure :: 3rd figure : ?

SOLUTION

• In the left pair the line-figure gains extra terminal markers and is re-oriented (the single-stem 'T' becomes the double-ended bar).

• The 3rd figure is a diagonal line with one circle at its end; applying the same rule adds circles so the line carries markers at both ends and the middle (three equally-spaced circles) with the diagonal reflected.

• Only Option shows a '\' diagonal with three equally-spaced circles; option has the wrong ('/') orientation and options 1–2 have only two circles.

• Hence the missing figure = Option.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Count the circles and check the diagonal's slant: the answer must be the three-circle '\' figure.

NOTE

• For line-and-node figures, track (a) number of nodes and (b) orientation of the line separately.

question: Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. the box with 'B C E' in the top row and 'A  D' in the bottom row.

GIVEN

• Box1 (M 8 / 4 / T 7) : Box2 (8 4 7 / M T) :: Box3 (A B / C / D E) : ?

SOLUTION

• Label the source positions: TL, TR, centre, BL, BR.

• Box1→Box2 rule: top row of the result = (TR, centre, BR) = 8,4,7; bottom row = (TL, BL) = M,T. ✓

• Apply to Box3 (TL=A, TR=B, centre=C, BL=D, BR=E): top row = (TR, centre, BR) = B, C, E; bottom row = (TL, BL) = A, D.

• Result = top 'B C E', bottom 'A  D' = Option.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Right column + centre move to the top row, left column moves to the bottom row: B,C,E over A,D.

NOTE

• For grid-rearrangement figures, fix a position map from the sample pair and reapply it to the target box.

question:
Select the option that is related to the second letter-number cluster in the same way as the third letter-number cluster is related to the fourth letter-number cluster and fifth letter-number cluster is related to sixth letter-number cluster.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

? : TH20 :: PE12 : OC24 :: DK18 : CI36
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. UJ10.

GIVEN

• ? : TH20 :: PE12 : OC24 :: DK18 : CI36

SOLUTION

• Rule (1st→2nd cluster): 1st letter −1, 2nd letter −2, number ×2.

• Check PE12→OC24: P−1=O, E−2=C, 12×2=24. ✓

• Check DK18→CI36: D−1=C, K−2=I, 18×2=36. ✓

• Reverse from TH20: 1st = T+1 = U; 2nd = H+2 = J; number = 20÷2 = 10.

• So ? = UJ10.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• The answer maps to TH20 by −1, −2, ×2 — so undo it: T+1=U, H+2=J, 20/2=10.

NOTE

• Treat letters (position ±k) and the number (×/÷) with separate rules; operate on the whole number.

question:
Select the option that is related to the sixth letter-number cluster in the same way as the first letter-number cluster is related to the second letter-number cluster and third letter-number cluster is related to fourth letter-number cluster.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. ZWX42 : BBD84 :: ALP61 : CQV122 :: ? : LMT92
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. JHN46.

• ZWX42 : BBD84 :: ALP61 : CQV122 :: ? : LMT92

SOLUTION

• Rule (1st→2nd cluster): letters +2, +5, +6 (cyclic), number ×2.

• Check ALP61→CQV122: A+2=C, L+5=Q, P+6=V, 61×2=122. ✓

• Reverse from LMT92: 1st = L−2 = J; 2nd = M−5 = H; 3rd = T−6 = N; number = 92÷2 = 46.

• The answer becomes LMT92 by +2,+5,+6,×2 — reverse it: L−2=J, M−5=H, T−6=N, 92/2=46.

NOTE

• Apply a fixed shift to each letter position and a single arithmetic operation to the whole number.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and fourth number is related to third number.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

9739 : 9697 :: 5302 : 5260 :: 4086 : ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 4044.

GIVEN

• 9739 : 9697 :: 5302 : 5260 :: 4086 : ?

SOLUTION

• Rule: 2nd number = 1st number − 42.

• Check: 9739 − 42 = 9697 ✓; 5302 − 42 = 5260 ✓.

• Apply: 4086 − 42 = 4044.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Same constant subtraction throughout: just do 4086 − 42 = 4044.

NOTE

• First find the fixed difference from a known pair, then apply it to the target number.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fourth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and fifth number is related to sixth number.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

974 : 484 :: ? : 214 :: 1012 : 503
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 434.

GIVEN

• 974 : 484 :: ? : 214 :: 1012 : 503

SOLUTION

• Rule (1st→2nd): 2nd = (1st ÷ 2) − 3.

• Check 974: 974÷2 = 487, 487−3 = 484 ✓; 1012: 1012÷2 = 506, 506−3 = 503 ✓.

• Reverse from 214: ? = (214 + 3) × 2 = 217 × 2 = 434.

• Verify: 434÷2 = 217, 217−3 = 214 ✓.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Undo the rule on 214: add 3 then double → (214+3)×2 = 434.

NOTE

• When the target is the 'first' side of the relation, invert the operations (÷2 then −3 becomes +3 then ×2).

question: In a certain coded language 'FERAL' is coded as 'GFVXG' and 'SMEAR' is coded as 'TNIXM'. How will 'PHOTO' be coded in the same code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. QISQJ.

GIVEN

• FERAL → GFVXG, SMEAR → TNIXM. Find PHOTO.

SOLUTION

• Position-wise shifts are fixed: +1, +1, +4, −3, −5.

• Check FERAL: F+1=G, E+1=F, R+4=V, A−3=X (cyclic), L−5=G. ✓

• Check SMEAR: S+1=T, M+1=N, E+4=I, A−3=X, R−5=M. ✓

• Apply to PHOTO: P+1=Q, H+1=I, O+4=S, T−3=Q, O−5=J → QISQJ.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Memorise the 5-slot shift pattern +1,+1,+4,−3,−5 and apply letter by letter.

NOTE

• Each position can have its own shift; wrap cyclically when you go past A or Z.

question: In a certain code language, 'SING' is coded as '57' and 'FAIR' is coded as '72'. How will 'PARTY' be coded in that code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 53.

GIVEN

• SING → 57, FAIR → 72. Find PARTY.

SOLUTION

• Use reverse letter values (A=26, B=25, …, Z=1), i.e. value = 27 − position. Code = (sum of reverse values) − 2.

• SING = 8+18+13+20 = 59 → 59 − 2 = 57 ✓.

• FAIR = 21+26+18+9 = 74 → 74 − 2 = 72 ✓.

• PARTY = P(11)+A(26)+R(9)+T(7)+Y(2) = 55 → 55 − 2 = 53.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Add reverse-alphabet values (27 − position) of all letters, then subtract 2: PARTY = 55 − 2 = 53.

NOTE

• When forward-position sums fail, test reverse values (A=26…Z=1); a constant offset often completes the code.

question:
A series is given with one term wrong. Select that wrong term from the given alternatives.

DL216, FH343, HD512, KZ720, LV1000, NR1331
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. KZ720.

GIVEN

• DL216, FH343, HD512, KZ720, LV1000, NR1331

SOLUTION

• Numbers should be consecutive cubes: 6³=216, 7³=343, 8³=512, 9³=729, 10³=1000, 11³=1331.

• The 4th term shows 720, but it must be 729 → so KZ720 is wrong.

• Also 1st letters go D, F, H, J, L, N (+2 each), so the 4th should start with J, not K — confirming the 4th term is faulty.

• Wrong term = KZ720.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Spot the cubes 6³…11³; 720 isn't a cube (9³ = 729), so KZ720 is the odd one out.

NOTE

• Check the numeric tail against a known pattern (cubes/squares) first — it usually exposes the wrong term instantly.

question:
A series is given with one term wrong. Select that wrong term from the given alternatives.

CAT5, DEA124, EIH243, FNP362, GQV481, HUC600
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. FNP362.

GIVEN

• CAT5, DEA124, EIH243, FNP362, GQV481, HUC600

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: C, D, E, F, G, H (+1 each). ✓

• 2nd letters should be A, E, I, M, Q, U (+4 each) — but the 4th shows N instead of M.

• 3rd letters should be T, A, H, O, V, C (+7 cyclic) — but the 4th shows P instead of O.

• Numbers 5, 124, 243, 362, 481, 600 (+119 each) are fine, so the letters expose the error: 4th term should be FMO362.

• Wrong term = FNP362.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• 2nd letter jumps by 4 and 3rd by 7; the 4th term breaks both (N,P instead of M,O), so FNP362 is wrong.

NOTE

• Verify each letter column and the number column separately with constant differences to catch the faulty term.
